questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII, what is the safest first step when classifying a building?

options.text: Identify the proposed use or character of occupancy and match it to the listed Group A to J classification.
Start with the preferred structural material.
Choose the group with the lowest permit fee.
Classify all buildings as commercial unless residential units are present.

questions.rationale: Rule VII classifies buildings by proposed use or character of occupancy before downstream requirements are applied.

questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes Group A from Group B in the checked PD 1096 source?

options.text: Group A includes listed residential dwellings and A-2 non-leasing occupants not exceeding ten persons; Group B covers similar residential, hotel, and apartment uses accommodating more than ten persons.
Group A is only hotels while Group B is only single-family houses.
Group A and Group B are separated only by building height.
Group B applies only when the structure is industrial.

questions.rationale: The checked source places the ten-person line between A-2 non-leasing residential uses and Group B residential, hotel, and apartment occupancies.

questions.text: For mixed occupancy under PD 1096 Rule VII, what is the default rule?

options.text: Apply the most restrictive requirement among the occupancies present unless a checked exception applies.
Apply only the requirement for the largest floor area.
Ignore minor occupancies even when they exceed ten percent.
Average the requirements of all occupancies.

questions.rationale: PD 1096 states that a mixed-occupancy building is subject to the most restrictive requirement unless the one-storey or minor-accessory exception applies.

questions.text: Which minor accessory-use condition is source-safe under PD 1096 Rule VII?

options.text: The accessory use must not occupy more than ten percent of the area of any floor and not more than ten percent of the basic area permitted in the occupancy requirement.
The accessory use may occupy up to half of any floor.
The accessory use automatically controls the whole building.
The accessory use is ignored only if it is on the roof.

questions.rationale: The checked mixed-occupancy exception uses the ten percent threshold for the area of any floor and the basic area permitted.

questions.text: Which assembly classification statement is source-safe from PD 1096 Rule VII?

options.text: Group I is an assembly building with a stage and an occupant load of one thousand or more.
Group I is every assembly space over one hundred occupants.
Group H is only outdoor stadiums.
Stage presence is irrelevant to Group I.

questions.rationale: The checked source identifies Group I as any assembly building with a stage and an occupant load of one thousand or more.

questions.text: For mixed occupancy under PD 1096 Rule VII, what is the default rule?

options.text: Apply the most restrictive requirement among the occupancies present unless a checked exception applies.
Apply only the requirement for the largest floor area.
Ignore minor occupancies even when they exceed ten percent.

questions.rationale: PD 1096 states that a mixed-occupancy building is subject to the most restrictive requirement unless the one-storey or minor-accessory exception applies.
questions.explanation: The 10-person cutoff is one of the most frequently tested distinctions on the LEA. Group A Div. 2 → Group B is triggered the moment the non-leasing residential population exceeds 10, regardless of building type.

questions.text: Which minor accessory-use condition is source-safe under PD 1096 Rule VII?

options.text: The accessory use must not occupy more than ten percent of the area of any floor and not more than ten percent of the basic area permitted in the occupancy requirement.
The accessory use may occupy up to half of any floor.
The accessory use automatically controls the whole building.
The accessory use is ignored only if it is on the roof.

questions.rationale: The checked mixed-occupancy exception uses the ten percent threshold for the area of any floor and the basic area permitted.
questions.explanation: Two exceptions exist under Sec. 703: (a) one-storey buildings may treat each portion under its own occupancy; (b) accessory uses occupying not more than 10% of any storey may allow the major occupancy to govern.

questions.text: Which assembly classification statement is source-safe from PD 1096 Rule VII?

options.text: Group I is an assembly building with a stage and an occupant load of one thousand or more.
Group I is every assembly space over one hundred occupants.
Group H is only outdoor stadiums.
Stage presence is irrelevant to Group I.

questions.rationale: The checked source identifies Group I as any assembly building with a stage and an occupant load of one thousand or more.
questions.explanation: The dual condition (stage AND occupant load ≥ 1,000) is the most common Group I classification trap. Missing either condition drops the classification to the appropriate Group H division.

questions.explanation: The 10% accessory-use exception prevents over-regulation of buildings that contain small subordinate uses. A small clinic, chapel, or daycare inside a mall need not reclassify the entire mall to institutional or religious standards if they occupy 10% or less of any storey.
